paragraphs: The Company was organized in 1918 and incorporated as a Pennsylvania business corporation in 1930. Quaker Houghton is the global leader in industrial process fluids. With a robust presence around the world, including operations in over 25 countries, the Company's customers include thousands of the world's most advanced and specialized steel, aluminum, automotive, aerospace, offshore, can, mining, and metalworking companies. Quaker Houghton develops, produces, and markets a broad range of formulated specialty chemical products and offers chemical management services (which we refer to as "FluidcareTM") for various heavy industrial and manufacturing applications throughout its three segments: Americas; Europe, Middle East and Africa ("EMEA"); and Asia/Pacific.

The major product lines of Quaker Houghton include metal removal fluids, cleaning fluids, corrosion inhibitors, metal drawing and forming fluids, die cast mold releases, heat treatment and quenchants, metal forging fluids, hydraulic fluids, surface solutions, specialty greases, offshore sub-sea energy control fluids, rolling lubricants, and rod and wire drawing fluids. The following are the respective contributions to consolidated net sales of each of our principal product lines representing more than 10% of consolidated net sales for any of the past three years based on the Company's current product line segmentation:
Metal removal fluids 19.0 % 22.4 % 23.6 % Rolling lubricants 18.3 % 20.5 % 19.5 % Hydraulic fluids 12.2 % 14.2 % 14.1 %
Surface solutions 10.9 % 5.2 % 5.0 % Sales Revenue

The majority of the Company's sales worldwide are made directly through its own employees and its FluidcareTM programs, with the balance sold through distributors and agents. The Company's employees typically visit the plants of customers regularly, work on site, and through training and experience, identify production needs which can be resolved or otherwise addressed either by utilizing the Company's existing products or by applying new formulations developed in its laboratories.

As part of the Company's FluidcareTM business, certain third-party product sales to customers are managed by the Company. Where the Company acts as principal, revenues are recognized on a gross reporting basis at the selling price negotiated with its customers. Where the Company acts as an agent for its customers, revenue is recognized on a net reporting basis at the amount of the administrative fee earned by the Company for ordering the goods. See Note 5, Net Sales and Revenue Recognition, to the Consolidated Financial Statements for more information.

The specialty chemical industry comprises a number of companies similar in size to Quaker Houghton, as well as companies larger and smaller in size. The Company cannot readily determine its precise competitive position in every industry it serves. However, the Company estimates it holds the leading global position in the market for industrial process fluids including leading global positions in the markets for process fluids in portions of the automotive and industrial markets, and a leading position in the market for process fluids to produce sheet steel and aluminum. The offerings of many of the Company's competitors differ from those of Quaker Houghton; some offer a broad portfolio of fluids, including general lubricants, while others have more specialized product ranges. All competitors provide different levels of technical services to individual customers. Competition in the industry is based primarily on the ability to supply products and provide technical services that meet the needs of the customer at an appropriate price and value to both the Company and the customer.

In 2025, Quaker Houghton's five largest customers (each composed of multiple subsidiaries or divisions with semi-autonomous purchasing authority) accounted for approximately 11% of consolidated net sales, with its largest customer accounting for approximately 3% of consolidated net sales. A significant portion of the Company's revenues are realized from the sale of process fluids and services to manufacturers of steel, aluminum, automotive, aerospace, industrial equipment, and durable goods, and therefore, Quaker Houghton is subject to the same business cycles as those experienced by these manufacturers and their customers.

The Company's financial performance is generally correlated to the volume of global production within the industries it serves, rather than directly related to the financial performance of its customers. Furthermore, steel and aluminum customers typically have limited manufacturing locations compared to metalworking customers and generally use higher volumes of products at a single location.

Quaker Houghton uses approximately 3,000 raw materials, including animal fats, vegetable oils, mineral oils, oleochemicals, surfactant agents and various chemical compounds that act as additives to our base formulations. Quaker Houghton uses a significant number of raw materials derived from crude oil and natural gas. Other than of mineral oils, most of these raw material inputs are fourth to sixth generation derivatives of crude oil and natural gas, which are subject to volatile oil and gas prices and can cause significant variations in our raw materials costs. Oleochemicals are impacted by their own unique supply and demand factors. As experienced during 2025 and 2024, the Company's earnings have been and could continue to be affected by market changes in raw material prices. Refer to the disclosure contained in Item 7A of this Report for additional information.

Quaker Houghton has a limited number of patents and patent applications including patents issued, applied for, or acquired in the U.S. and in various foreign countries, some of which may be material to its business, with the earliest patent expiry in 2026. The Company principally relies on its proprietary formulas and its applications know-how and experience to meet customer needs. Quaker Houghton products are identified by numerous trademarks that are registered throughout its marketing area.

The Company maintains approximately 30 separate laboratory facilities worldwide that are primarily devoted to applied research and development. In addition, the Company maintains quality control labs at each of its manufacturing facilities. Quaker Houghton research and development is directed primarily toward applied technology since the nature of the Company's business requires continual modification and improvement of formulations to provide specialty chemicals to satisfy customer requirements. If problems are encountered which cannot be resolved by local laboratories, the problem is referred to one of our 10 principal laboratories, located in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania; Valley Forge, Pennsylvania; Aurora, Illinois; Santa Fe Springs, California; Uithoorn, Netherlands; Coventry, United Kingdom; Dortmund, Germany; Barcelona, Spain; Turin, Italy or Qingpu, China.

Research and development costs are expensed as incurred. Research and development expenses during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023 were $60.7 million, $57.3 million and $50.3 million, respectively.

In April 2025, the Company acquired Dipsol Chemicals Co., Ltd. and its subsidiaries, ("Dipsol"). Dipsol is headquartered in Japan and is a leading supplier of surface treatment and plating solutions and services primarily for the automotive and other industrial applications end markets. Dipsol has operations in several countries and these operations are reported within the Company's respective Americas, EMEA, and Asia/Pacific segments. This acquisition expands the Company's advanced solutions businesses in attractive end markets with solid growth characteristics. Dipsol also provides significant cross-selling opportunities and enhances the Company's ability to meet the needs of our customers across the globe.

headings: Risks Related to the Demand for our Products and Services and our Customer Base
Changes to the industries and markets that we serve could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
Changes in competition in the industries and markets we serve could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
Risks Related to Business Operations, Including Internal and External Factors that May Impact Our Operational Continuity
The timing and amount of the Company's share repurchases are subject to a number of uncertainties, and there can be no assurance that we will continue to repurchase shares of our common stock.

Failure to comply with any material provision of our principal credit facility or other debt agreements could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
Risks Related to our International Operations
Our global presence subjects us to political and economic risks that could adversely affect our business, liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
The scope of our international operations subjects us to risks from currency fluctuations that could adversely affect our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
Risks Relating to Our Supply Chain
We rely on a wide variety of raw materials, and our business depends on our ability to source them cost-effectively.

Loss of a significant manufacturing facility or disruptions within our supply chain or in transportation could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
Risks Relating to Domestic and Foreign Taxation and Government Regulation and Oversight
Changes in tax laws could result in fluctuations in our effective tax rate and have a material effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.
We are subject to stringent labor and employment laws in the jurisdictions in which we operate, and our relationship with our employees could deteriorate which could adversely impact our operations.
General Risk Factors
Our business could be adversely affected by environmental, health and safety laws and regulations or by potential product, service or other related liability claims.
Our insurance may not fully cover all potential exposures.

Disruption of critical information systems or material breaches in the security of our systems could adversely affect our business and our customer relationships and subject us to fines or other regulatory actions.
paragraphs: There are many factors that may affect our business and results of operations, including the following risks relating to: (1) the demand for our products and services and our ability to grow our customer base; (2) our business operations, including internal and external factors that may impact our operational continuity; (3) our international operations; (4) our supply chain; (5) domestic and foreign taxation and government regulation and oversight; and (6) more general risk factors that may impact our business.

As the leader in industrial process fluids, we are subject to the same business cycles as those experienced by our customers that participate in the steel, automotive, industrial equipment, aerospace, aluminum and durable goods industries. Because demand for our products and services is largely derived from the global demand for our customers' products, we are subject to uncertainties related to downturns in our customers' businesses and shutdowns or curtailments of our customers' production, including as a result of adverse changes affecting national, regional and global economies or increased competitive pressure within our customers' industries. Our customers may experience deterioration of their businesses, cash flow shortages and difficulty obtaining financing, leading them to delay or cancel plans to purchase products, and they may not be able to pay our bills or fulfill their other obligations in a timely fashion. We have limited ability to adjust our costs contemporaneously with changes in sales; thus, a significant sudden downturn in sales or increased credit losses due to reductions in global production within the industries we serve and/or weak end-user markets could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations. Further, our suppliers and other business partners may experience similar conditions, which could impact their ability to fulfill their obligations to us and also result in material adverse effects on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.

The specialty chemical industry is highly competitive and there are many companies with significant financial resources and/or customer relationships that compete with us to provide similar products and services. Some competitors may be able to offer more favorable or flexible pricing and service terms or may be better able to adapt to changes in conditions in our industries, fluctuations in the costs of raw materials or to changes in global economic conditions, potentially resulting in reduced profitability and/or a loss of market share for us. The pricing decisions of our competitors could affect demand for our offerings, and could lead us to decrease our prices, which could negatively affect our margins and profitability. In addition, our competitors could potentially consolidate their businesses and gain scale or better position their product offerings, which could have a negative impact on our profitability and market share. Competition in our industry historically has also been based on the ability to provide products that meet the needs of the customer and render technical services and laboratory assistance, which our competitors may be able to accomplish more effectively or efficiently than we can. If we are unsuccessful with differentiating ourselves, it could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations and we could lose market share to our competitors.

Loss of a significant customer, bankruptcy of a major customer, or the closure of or significant reduction in production at a customer site could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.

During 2025, our top five largest customers (each composed of multiple subsidiaries or divisions with semi-autonomous purchasing authority) together accounted for approximately 11% of our consolidated net sales, with the largest customer accounting for approximately 3% of our consolidated net sales. The loss of a significant customer could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations. Also, a significant portion of our revenues is derived from sales to customers in the cyclical steel, aerospace, aluminum and automotive industries, where bankruptcies have occurred in the past and where companies have periodically experienced financial difficulties. If a significant customer or group of customers in the same industry experiences financial difficulties or files for bankruptcy protection, we may be unable to collect on our receivables, customer manufacturing sites may be closed, or our contracts may be voided, which could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and result of operations. The bankruptcy of a major customer could therefore have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, financial position and results of operations. Also, some of our customers, primarily in the steel, aluminum and aerospace industries, often have fewer manufacturing locations compared to other metalworking customers and generally use higher volumes of products at a single location. The loss, closure, or significant reduction in production at one or more of these locations or other major sites of a significant customer could have a material adverse effect on our business.

We may not be able to timely develop, manufacture and gain market acceptance of new and enhanced products required to maintain or expand our business, which could adversely affect our competitive position and our liquidity, financial position and results of operations.

paragraphs: Quaker Houghton is the global leader in industrial process fluids. With a presence around the world, including operations in over 25 countries, our customers include thousands of the world's most advanced and specialized steel, aluminum, automotive, aerospace, offshore, container, mining, and metalworking companies. Our high-performing, innovative and sustainable solutions are backed by best-in-class technology, deep process knowledge, and customized services. Quaker Houghton is headquartered in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania, located near Philadelphia in the U.S.

Net sales of $1,888.6 million in 2025 increased 3% compared to $1,839.7 million in 2024. The net sales increase of $48.9 million, or 3%, is primarily due to contributions from acquisitions of approximately 4% and favorable foreign currency translation of approximately 1%, partially offset by decreases in selling price and product mix of approximately 2%. Organic sales volumes remained consistent in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily as a result of continued new business wins across all segments, particularly Asia/Pacific, which was offset by a continuation of soft end market conditions including the uncertainty caused by tariffs, particularly in the Americas and EMEA segments. The decrease in selling price and product mix was primarily attributable to the impact of the mix of products, services and geographies and the impact of our index-based customer contracts.

The Company reported a net loss of $2.5 million or $0.14 net loss per diluted share in 2025, compared to a net income of $116.6 million or $6.51 earnings per diluted share in 2024. The net loss primarily reflects an $88.8 million non-cash impairment charge to write down the remaining value of goodwill associated with the Company's EMEA reportable segment. Excluding non-recurring and non-core items, the Company's current year non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP earnings per diluted share were $123.2 million and $7.02, respectively, compared to $133.5 million and $7.44, respectively, in 2024. The decrease in current year Non-GAAP earnings was primarily driven by lower gross margins and an increase in selling, general and administrative expenses ("SG&A"), partially offset by an increase in net sales. The Company generated adjusted EBITDA of $299.2 million compared to $310.9 million in 2024, as the increase in net sales was offset by lower operating margins and an increase in SG&A. Non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP earnings per diluted share and adjusted EBITDA are non-GAAP measures. See "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Results of Operations—Consolidated—Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" for the definition and reconciliation of these measures to their most comparable GAAP measures.

The Company's 2025 operating performance in each of its three reportable segments: (i) Americas; (ii) EMEA; and (iii) Asia/Pacific, reflects similar drivers to that of the Company's consolidated performance. The increase in operating earnings for the Asia/Pacific segment compared to the prior year was primarily driven by an increase in net sales and further contribution from acquisitions, partially offset by lower segment operating margins. The decrease in operating earnings for the EMEA segment compared to the prior year was primarily driven by lower segment operating margins, partially offset by an increase in net sales. The decrease in operating earnings for the America segment compared to the prior year was primarily driven by a decrease in net sales and a decrease in segment operating margins. Additional details of segment operating performance are provided in the Reportable Segments Review in the Operations section of this Item below.

Net cash flows provided by operating activities were $136.5 million in 2025 compared to $204.6 million in 2024. The decrease in net operating cash flows was primarily driven by lower operating performance, higher cash outflows from restructuring activities and higher outflows from working capital in 2025 compared to 2024. The key drivers of the Company's operating cash flow and working capital are further discussed in the Company's Liquidity and Capital Resources section of this Item 7, below.

The Company performed well in 2025, making progress on its long-term financial and strategic initiatives. In addition, the Company results in 2025 reflect an increase in sales volumes in the Asia/Pacific segment and new business wins across all segments, despite a continuation of challenging end market conditions, particularly in the Americas and EMEA segments.

On July 4, 2025, H.R. 1, commonly known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the "OBBB"), was signed into law. The OBBB includes significant changes to the federal corporate tax provisions and extends certain otherwise expiring provisions of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Among other things, the legislation restores 100% bonus depreciation for eligible property, reinstates expensing for domestic research and experimental expenditures, imposes new limitations on interest expense deductibility, and expands disallowed deductions for certain employee remuneration. The legislation has multiple effective dates, with certain provisions effective in 2025 and other provisions implemented through 2027. The provisions effective in 2025 do not have a material impact to our consolidated financial statements. The Company is continuing to evaluate the potential impacts of the provisions effective in 2026 and 2027.

paragraphs: 本公司於1918年成立，並於1930年在賓夕法尼亞州登記為商業公司。Quaker Houghton為工業製程流體的全球領導者。本公司在全球擁有強大的業務據點，包括在超過25個國家的運營，其客戶包括數千家世界上最先進且專業的鋼鐵、鋁、汽車、航空、離岸、罐頭、礦業及金屬加工公司。Quaker Houghton開發、生產並行銷廣泛的配方專用化學產品，並為各種重工業及製造應用提供化學管理服務（我們稱為"FluidcareTM"），透過其三個應報告分部：美洲；歐洲、中東及非洲（"EMEA"）；以及亞洲/太平洋。
Quaker Houghton的主要產品線包括金屬去除流體、清潔流體、腐蝕抑制劑、金屬拉拔與成型流體、壓鑄模具釋放劑、熱處理與淬火劑、金屬鍛造流體、液壓流體、表面解決方案、特殊潤滑脂、離岸海底能源控制流體、軋製潤滑劑，以及棒材與線材拉拔流體。以下為各主要產品線對合併淨銷售額的貢獻，代表過去三年中任一年度合併淨銷售額超過10%的產品線，根據本公司目前的產品線分類：
表面解決方案 10.9 % 5.2 % 5.0 % 營業收入
本公司全球銷售的絕大多數透過其員工及FluidcareTM方案直接進行，餘下部分則透過經銷商及代理商銷售。本公司員工通常會定期訪問客戶工廠，現場工作，並透過培訓與經驗，識別可透過本公司現有產品解決或透過其實驗室開發的新配方解決的生產需求。
作為本公司FluidcareTM業務的一部分，某些第三方產品銷售由本公司管理。當本公司作為主要責任方時，收入以銷售價格與客戶協議的總計方式確認。當本公司作為客戶的代理人時，收入以本公司收取的行政費用金額為基礎，以淨額方式確認。有關更多資訊，請參閱財務報表附註5，淨銷售額與收入確認。

特殊化學產業包含許多與Quaker Houghton規模相近的公司，以及規模較大或較小的公司。本公司無法輕易確定其在所服務每個產業中的精確競爭地位。然而，本公司估計其在工業製程流體市場中擁有領先的全球地位，包括在汽車及工業市場部分領域的製程流體市場中擁有領先的全球地位，以及在製造鋼板與鋁的製程流體市場中擁有領先地位。許多競爭對手的產品與Quaker Houghton不同；有些提供廣泛的流體產品組合，包括一般潤滑劑，而有些則有較為專業的產品範圍。所有競爭對手均提供不同層級的技術服務給個別客戶。產業競爭主要基於能否供應產品並提供技術服務，以符合客戶需求，同時對本公司與客戶而言具有適當的價格與價值。
2025年，Quaker Houghton的五大客戶（每家均由多個子公司或部門組成，具有半自主的採購權限）約佔合併淨銷售額的11%，其中最大的客戶約佔合併淨銷售額的3%。本公司相當大的收入來自向鋼鐵、鋁、汽車、航空、工業設備及耐用消費品製造商銷售製程流體與服務，因此，Quaker Houghton與這些製造商及其客戶經歷相同的商業週期。
本公司的財務表現通常與其服務產業的全球生產量相關，而非直接與其客戶的財務表現相關。此外，鋼鐵與鋁合金客戶通常較金屬加工客戶擁有較少的製造據點，且通常在單一據點使用較大量的產品。

Quaker Houghton 使用約 3,000 種原料，包括動物脂肪、植物油、礦物油、油脂化學製品、表面活性劑及各種化學化合物，這些化學化合物作為我們基礎配方的添加劑。Quaker Houghton 使用大量來自原油與天然氣的原料。除了礦物油外，這些原料大多為原油與天然氣的第四至第六代衍生物，這些原料價格波動較大，可能導致我們的原料成本出現顯著變動。油脂化學製品受其獨特的供需因素影響。如 2025 年及 2024 年所經驗，本公司獲利可能已並可能持續受到原料價格市場變動的影響。有關更多資訊，請參閱本報告第 7A 項所載的揭露內容。
Quaker Houghton 擁有少量的專利與專利申請，包括美國及各國發行、申請或取得的專利，其中一些可能對其業務具有重大影響，最早到期的專利為 2026 年。本公司主要依賴其專利配方及應用知識與經驗來滿足客戶需求。Quaker Houghton 產品以多項商標識別，並在行銷區域內註冊。

本公司在全球維護約 30 個獨立的實驗室，主要用於應用研究與開發。此外，本公司在每個製造廠設有品質控制實驗室。Quaker Houghton 的研究與開發主要針對應用技術，因本公司業務性質需要持續修改與改進配方，以提供特殊化學品以符合客戶需求。若遇到無法由當地實驗室解決的問題，會轉交至我們的 10 個主要實驗室，分別位於賓夕法尼亞州康紹克肯、賓夕法尼亞州瓦利福爾奇、伊利諾州奧羅拉、加州聖菲斯普林斯、荷蘭烏伊託倫、英國考文垂、德國多特蒙德、西班牙巴塞羅那、義大利都靈或中國青浦。
研究與開發成本於發生時即計入費用。2025 年 12 月 31 日為結算日的各年度研究與開發費用分別為 60.7 百萬美元、57.3 百萬美元及 50.3 百萬美元。

2025 年 4 月，本公司取得 Dipsol Chemicals Co., Ltd. 及其子公司（"Dipsol"）。Dipsol 總部設於日本，是表面處理與電鍍解決方案與服務的主要供應商，主要服務於汽車及其他工業應用終端市場。Dipsol 在多個國家設有營運據點，這些營運據點歸入本公司各自的美洲、歐洲、中東及非洲（EMEA）及亞太（Asia/Pacific）分部。此項收購擴大了本公司在具備穩健成長特質的優勢終端市場的先進解決方案業務。Dipsol 也提供重要的交叉銷售機會，並增強本公司在全球範圍內滿足客戶需求的能力。

paragraphs: Quaker Houghton 是工業過程流體的全球領導者。公司在全球多個國家設有據點，包括在超過 25 個國家的業務，客戶包括數千家世界上最先進且專業的鋼鐵、鋁合金、汽車、航空、離岸、容器、採礦及金屬加工公司。我們高績效、創新且可持續的解決方案，背後有最佳等級的技術、深厚的製程知識及客製化服務。Quaker Houghton 董事會所在地為賓夕法尼亞州康紹克肯，位於美國費城附近。

2025 年淨銷售額為 1,888.6 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 1,839.7 百萬美元成長 3%。淨銷售額成長 48.9 百萬美元，或 3%，主要係因收購貢獻約 4% 以及有利的外幣兌換約 1%，部分抵銷因銷售價格及產品組成下降約 2%。2025 年的自有銷售量與 2024 年保持一致，主要係因各個業務部門持續獲得新業務，特別是亞太地區，但受到終端市場條件疲軟的影響，包括因關稅造成的不確定性，特別是在美洲及 EMEA 業務部門。

本公司在 2025 年報告淨虧損為 2.5 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後淨虧損 0.14 美元，較 2024 年的淨收入 116.6 百萬美元，或每股稀釋後 earnings 6.51 美元為負。淨虧損主要反映因本公司 EMEA 應報告分部的商譽減值非現金費用 88.8 百萬美元。排除非經常性及非核心項目後，本公司 2025 年非 GAAP 淨收入及非 GAAP 每股稀釋後 earnings 分別為 123.2 百萬美元及 7.02 美元，較 2024 年的 133.5 百萬美元及 7.44 美元為低。2025 年非 GAAP earnings 下降主要因毛利率下降及銷售、一般及行政費用（"SG&A"）增加，部分抵銷因淨銷售額增加。本公司產生調整後 EBITDA 為 299.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 310.9 百萬美元為低，因淨銷售額增加被較低的營運毛利率及 SG&A 增加所抵銷。非 GAAP 淨收入、非 GAAP 每股稀釋後 earnings 及調整後 EBITDA 為非 GAAP 財務指標。請參閱 "項目 7. 管理層對財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析—營運成果—綜合—非 GAAP 財務指標的使用" 以取得這些指標的定義及與其最相近 GAAP 財務指標的對應關係。

本公司 2025 年各三個應報告分部：(i) 美洲；(ii) EMEA；及 (iii) 亞太地區的營運表現，反映與本公司綜合營運表現相似的驅動因素。亞太地區分部的營運獲利較前一年增加，主要因淨銷售額增加及進一步收購貢獻，部分抵銷因分部營運毛利率下降。EMEA 分部的營運獲利較前一年下降，主要因分部營運毛利率下降，部分抵銷因淨銷售額增加。美洲分部的營運獲利較前一年下降，主要因淨銷售額下降及分部營運毛利率下降。有關分部營運表現的更多細節請參閱本項目 "營運" 部分的 "應報告分部審閱" 部分。
2025 年營運活動產生的現金流量為 136.5 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 204.6 百萬美元為低。現金流量下降主要因營運表現較低、重組活動的現金流出增加及 2025 年營運週轉資金流出較 2024 年為高。本公司營運現金流量及營運週轉資金的關鍵驅動因素請參閱本項目 7 的 "流動性及資本運用" 部分。
本公司在 2025 年表現良好，並在長期財務及戰略計畫上取得進展。此外，2025 年的結果反映亞太地區銷售量增加及各個業務部門的新業務獲勝，即使面對持續的終端市場挑戰，特別是在美洲及 EMEA 業務部門。

2025 年 7 月 4 日，H.R. 1，常被稱為「一項大而美好的法案」（"One Big Beautiful Bill Act"，簡稱 "OBBB"）已簽署成為法律。OBBB 包含對聯邦公司稅條款的重大變更，並延長 2017 年稅改與就業法案中某些即將到期的條款。其中包含的內容包括恢復對符合資格資產的 100% 優先折舊、恢復對國內研究及實驗支出的費用化、對利息費用扣除額設立新的限制，以及擴大對某些員工報酬的不允許扣除項目。該法案有多個生效日期，部分條款於 2025 年生效，其他條款則於 2027 年前逐步實施。2025 年生效的條款對本公司綜合財務報表無重大影響。本公司持續評估 2026 年及 2027 年生效條款的潛在影響。

headings: 與我們產品及服務需求及客戶基礎相關的風險
所服務產業與市場的變動可能對我們的流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
所服務產業與市場的競爭變化可能對我們的流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
與我們營運相關的風險，包括可能影響我們營運持續性的內部與外部因素
本公司股票買回的時機與金額受到許多不確定因素影響，無法保證我們會持續買回本公司普通股股票。
未能遵守任何重大條款的主信貸協議或其他債務協議可能對我們的流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
與我們國際營運相關的風險
我們在全球的業務佈局使我們面臨政治與經濟風險，可能對我們的業務、流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們的國際業務範圍使我們面臨貨幣波動的風險，這些風險可能會對我們的流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
與我們供應鏈相關的風險
我們依賴多種原物料，且我們的業務取決於我們能否以具成本效益的方式取得這些原物料。
失去重要的製造設施或供應鏈或運輸中斷，可能會對我們的流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大不利影響。
與國內外稅務及政府監管與監督相關的風險
稅法的變更可能會導致我們的有效稅率波動，並對我們的流動性、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大影響。
我們在營運的司法管轄區面臨嚴格的勞動及就業法規，且我們與員工的關係可能惡化，這可能會對我們的營運產生不利影響。
一般風險因素
本公司業務可能因環境、健康及安全法規或潛在產品、服務或其他相關責任索賠而受到不利影響。
本公司保險可能無法完全覆蓋所有潛在風險暴露。
關鍵資訊系統中斷或系統安全遭重大違規，可能對本公司業務及客戶關係造成不利影響，並使本公司面臨罰款或其他監管措施。
paragraphs: 影響本公司業務及營運結果的因素甚多，包括下列風險：(1) 產品與服務的需求及擴大客戶羣的能力建立；(2) 本公司業務營運，包括內在與外在因素可能影響營運連續性；(3) 本公司國際業務營運；(4) 本公司供應鏈；(5) 國內與外國稅務及政府監管與監督；以及(6) 更一般性的風險因素可能影響本公司業務。

作為工業流程流體領域的領導者，本公司與參與鋼鐵、汽車、工業設備、航空、鋁與耐用商品產業的客戶一樣，經歷相同的商業週期。由於本公司產品與服務的需求大多來自於客戶產品的全球需求，因此本公司面臨客戶業務衰退與客戶生產停工或減產的不確定性，包括因國家、區域與全球經濟的不利變化或客戶產業內競爭壓力增加所導致的影響。客戶可能經歷業務惡化、現金流短缺與取得融資困難，導致延遲或取消購買產品的計畫，且客戶可能無法按時支付本公司應收款或履行其其他義務。本公司調整成本的能力有限，因此若銷售出現顯著且突然的衰退，或因所服務產業內全球生產減少導致信用損失增加，可能會對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。此外，本公司供應商及其他商業夥伴也可能經歷類似情況，這可能會影響他們履行對本公司義務的能力，並導致對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。

特殊化學品產業競爭激烈，且有許多擁有顯著財務資源與/或客戶關係的公司與本公司競爭，提供類似產品與服務。部分競爭對手可能能提供更優惠或更靈活的價格與服務條款，或更能適應本公司產業條件的變化、原材料成本波動或全球經濟條件的變化，這可能會導致本公司利潤減少與/或市場佔有率流失。競爭對手的價格決定可能影響本公司產品的需求，並導致本公司降低價格，這可能會對本公司毛利率與利潤造成負面影響。此外，競爭對手可能進行業務合併，取得規模優勢或更有效地定位其產品，這可能會對本公司利潤與市場佔有率造成負面影響。本公司產業的競爭歷來也基於提供符合客戶需求的產品與提供技術服務與實驗室協助的能力，而競爭對手可能比本公司更能有效地或高效地做到這一點。若本公司無法成功區隔自身，可能會對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響，並可能失去對競爭對手的市場佔有率。
失去重要客戶、重要客戶破產，或客戶廠區關閉或生產量大幅減少，可能會對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。

2025 年，本公司前五大客戶（每家均由多個子公司或部門組成，具有半自主採購權）合計約佔本公司合併淨銷售額的 11%，其中最大的客戶約佔本公司合併淨銷售額的 3%。失去重要客戶可能會對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。此外，本公司收入的很大一部分來自於銷售給鋼鐵、航空、鋁與汽車等週期性產業的客戶，這些產業過去曾發生過破產，且公司曾 periodically 面臨財務困難。若某重要客戶或同產業的客戶羣體遭遇財務困難或申請破產保護，本公司可能無法收回應收款，客戶製造廠區可能關閉，或本公司契約可能被取消，這可能會對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。重要客戶的破產因此可能對本公司流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。此外，部分客戶，尤其是鋼鐵、鋁與航空產業的客戶，通常製造廠區較少，與其他金屬加工客戶相比，通常在單一廠區使用較大量的產品。若這些廠區或重要客戶的其他主要廠區發生損失、關閉或生產量大幅減少，可能會對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能無法及時開發、製造並獲得市場接受度的新產品與增強型產品，以維持或擴展本公司業務，這可能會對本公司競爭地位與流動性、財務狀況與營運結果造成不利影響。
